_comment: Shipped enforcement example: merge the hooks block into the project's .claude/settings.json during adaptation. When a retro is due, the Stop hook emits a systemMessage that Claude Code shows to the user at the end of the turn; when the cadence is not due it stays silent; when the check itself errors (malformed ledger, wrong directory), it says so instead of misreporting a due retro. The command roots itself at $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR because hooks run in the session's current working directory and receipt.sh resolves its ledger from there. Exit-code stderr is unreliable for surfacing text (a non-blocking error shows only a first-line hook-error notice), so the hook uses JSON output instead.

hooks.command: if ! cd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then echo '{"systemMessage":"Harness hook could not resolve the project directory (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR)."}'; else bash scripts/receipt.sh check >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; if [ "$rc" -eq 1 ]; then echo '{"systemMessage":"Harness retro due: run scripts/receipt.sh check for details, then skills/retro."}'; elif [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then echo '{"systemMessage":"Harness receipt check errored; run scripts/receipt.sh check to see why."}'; fi; fi
